A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CASR research. All ten pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables and references. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: V2 reports original CASR evaluations on DIV8K, RealSR and CelebA-HQ, together with component, loss and superpixel-size ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: V4 retains these original benchmark evaluations and ablations, with revised BFSR comparison scores in Table 2.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same cyclic scaling procedure, SSAM and SARM components, SD-Turbo backbone, attention mechanisms, losses and two-stage training.

E1.justification: Both versions train on DF2K and evaluate on DIV8K, RealSR and CelebA-HQ. The magnification scenarios, including progressive upsampling, are unchanged.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain LINF, BFSR, IDM, Kim, LIIF+Diff and CiaoSR+Diff, with IDM and Kim retained for face evaluation. Revising BFSR's scores does not change comparator membership.

E3.justification: Sections 4.1–4.4 retain the same sampling, preprocessing, metrics, training settings and inference procedures, including 512×512 patches with 64-pixel overlap. No protocol revision is stated for the changed BFSR scores.

E4.justification: The progressive-cascade comparison and analyses of components, global semantic context, auxiliary losses and superpixel size remain unchanged, including Tables 4–7 and their qualitative examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V4 introduces no statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: All 15 BFSR scores in RealSR Table 2 change; v2's row exactly duplicates LINF's. For example, at ×8, MUSIQ/NIQE/PI changes from 19.58/11.50/9.96 to 18.27/9.91/8.96. Other reported results, including CASR's scores and leading position in Table 2, remain unchanged. The PDFs do not explain the revision.

T1.justification: The scale decomposition, superpixel representation, similarity matrices and loss definitions in Equations 1–7 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about stable single-model cyclic super-resolution, distribution alignment and self-similarity preservation. The added code link does not alter the scientific claims.

C2.justification: Interpretations of distribution drift, component effectiveness and global context are unchanged. Both retain the same qualification that larger superpixels can remove details or alter content, and the same proposed future applications.

D1.justification: V4 adds a GitHub source-code link in the abstract, providing access information absent from v2. Implementation details and hyperparameters are unchanged; the supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, research positioning and 36 cited works are unchanged. Reference 29's changed citation-page backlink reflects text reflow rather than a bibliographic or positioning change.

P1.justification: V4 adds one code-availability sentence to the abstract and updates the arXiv version/date annotation. The remaining prose, terminology and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract sentence causes limited column and page reflow across the opening pages. Internal hyperlinks change from muted blue to bright blue, and the new code link is magenta. Figures, captions and table structures remain unchanged; the Table 2 numerical revisions are covered under E6.

improvement.justification: V4 improves code discoverability and addresses an apparent reporting error by replacing the BFSR row that duplicated LINF in Table 2. These are limited documentation and reporting gains; the method and CASR's empirical support remain unchanged. The PDFs neither explain the score revision nor verify the linked code's contents.
